story.title: Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you

draft:
What if Wikipedia only covered the block you’re standing on?

I just read about Local Wikipedia—a hyper‑local knowledge base that pulls articles for everything within a half‑hour walk. The prototype shows how we can combine geofencing with crowd‑sourced content to make place‑specific information instantly relevant. Imagine a tourist discovering the story behind a historic doorway, or a city planner pulling localized data without sifting through city‑wide archives.

The idea forces us to rethink the scale of “knowledge graphs.” Instead of a monolithic, global corpus, we could have layered, context‑aware nodes that surface only what matters to a user’s immediate environment. The challenge will be maintaining quality and avoiding fragmented silos, but the upside—real‑time, place‑centric learning—feels like a natural evolution for AI‑augmented search.

Would a hyper‑local encyclopedia change how you explore your neighborhood or conduct research?
